chunks: And in the narration of Masʿadah ibn Ṣadaqah, he said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said:

A believer has seven rights over another believer, made obligatory upon him by Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: that he honor him in his regard, hold affection for him in his breast, support him with his wealth, forbid his backbiting, visit him in his illness, accompany his funeral, and say nothing about him after his death except good.

key_terms.الْمُوَاسَاةُ لَهُ فِي مَالِهِ: sharing one’s wealth with him and providing material support
key_terms.الْوُدُّ لَهُ فِي صَدْرِهِ: holding sincere affection for him in one’s heart
key_terms.بَعْدَ مَوْتِهِ إِلَّا خَيْرًا: speaking only good of him after his death
key_terms.حُقُوقٍ وَاجِبَةٍ: obligatory rights that must be fulfilled

ai.seo_question: What rights does one believer have over another in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith outlines seven obligatory rights that one believer owes another, emphasizing honor, inner affection, financial support, and protection of dignity. It presents social solidarity and respect for fellow believers as duties rooted in divine obligation.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5850 - In the narration of Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, the Messenger of Allah (swt) (peace and blessings be upon him and his family) said:

"A believer has seven rights over another believer, which are obligatory upon him by Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic: to respect him in his sight, to have affection for him in his heart, to assist him with his wealth, to prohibit speaking ill of him in his absence, to visit him when he is sick, to accompany his funeral, and to speak only good of him after his death."
